evidence.reason: The stale-checkout path only guards unpushed commits (lines 617-638), then runs non-forced `git worktree remove` at line 644. A non-forced worktree removal checks tracked/untracked status but does not protect ignored files, so an ignored file can be deleted when the removal succeeds. Because removal succeeds, the `onStaleRefresh` callback at lines 645-657 is never invoked, leaving no refusal or cleanup chance. This is a concrete data-loss defect in the existing stale-worktree cleanup behavior; the same omission is reported at line 782.
